mechanic: An alibi by the order of events: the suspect's leaving comes before the last time the thing was seen, and he had no way back. The events are told out of order and by relative times; the timeline puts them in order.
note: Spoilers. The logic written before the prose, in the shape sketched in docs/archipelago-plan.md (questions[].needs lists alternative sets of clues; here each question has one set). `frame` is what the narrator's own prose always carries; `clues` are the units that could be case files. `facts` names the world model's facts that realise a clue, `chain` the tellings that bring it.

frame.says: The cup was set on its shelf in the vestry after evensong; at nine the shelf was bare.

questions.asks: Was the cup taken before the gate lamp was lit, or after?

rules_out.before the lamp was lit: c.reed: the cup was on its shelf when the lamp was lit

rules_out.Silas Bell: c.reed puts the taking after the lamp was lit; c.hobb puts Bell on the water before it was lit and across the river after, with the only boat
rules_out.anyone without a key: c.reed (the door locked when the lamp was lit) and c.lock (never forced)
rules_out.the narrator: c.keys: his key was in his pocket (his own word)

clues.says: Bell, who had quarrelled with him, went out at the lych-gate with a sack over his shoulder, before the gate lamp was lit.

clues.source: Tam Reed, the lamplighter, to the narrator on Sunday night: what he saw as he lit the gate lamp
clues.says: The cup was on its shelf; the sexton was at the vestry door with his keys, locked it and went off.

clues.source: Old Hobb, the ferryman, to the narrator on Monday morning: his last crossing
clues.says: Bell came aboard as he cast off; they were in mid-river when the gate lamp was kindled; he landed Bell on the far bank at eight, and the boat, the only one on the water, lay there all night.
clues.note: The order of two events from different sources (the casting off, the lighting of the lamp) rests on one sentence of this clue.

clues.says: He unlocked the vestry door himself, and the lock had not been forced.
There are two keys to the vestry: his, in his pocket all the evening, and the sexton's.
